scope: Option definitions for the shared Java converter and its adapters. Integration is delivered by #76 and #77.

localization.scope: Interface only; German KDS FHIR content is independent of interface language.

values.dar: DAR token from the field catalogue

dar.tableCodes: arbitrary strings; no enumeration parsing; validate with the optional FHIR validator

contactAssignment.nextTimestampCandidate: try when previous candidate finds no matching contact
contactAssignment.genericEncounter: one case Encounter with no KDS contact-level claim when Encounter is enabled and all levels are disabled

documentReferenceStrategy.explicit-only: Preserve supplied encounter references; leave references absent when no encounter is supplied. Do not derive encounters from timestamps.
documentReferenceStrategy.fill-missing: Preserve supplied encounter references; derive missing references using patient, timestamp and selected contact level.
documentReferenceStrategy.timestamp-only: Recompute encounter references using patient, timestamp and selected contact level, replacing any supplied encounter references. Without a usable timestamp or match, omit references including supplied ones and report the reason.
documentReferenceStrategy.temporalConflict: In explicit-only and fill-missing modes preserve supplied references and report temporal conflicts.
documentReferenceStrategy.automaticLevelSelection: Contact level applies to automatic matching; explicitly supplied references are not reassigned to a different level.
documentReferenceStrategy.noneSelection: Omit encounter references regardless of strategy.
documentReferenceStrategy.noUsableTimestampOrMatch: Omit automatically derived references and report the reason.
documentReferenceStrategy.inputContactIdentity: An input encounter is identified by the combination of patient ID and case number, resolved against input contacts rather than only selected output resources. A case number belonging only to another patient is an unresolved contact for this patient.
documentReferenceStrategy.unresolvedInputContact: Report a supplied patient ID/case number combination that does not exist in the input. In preserving modes, do not treat an unresolved supplied contact as an absent selection and silently substitute an automatically matched contact.

order: source IDs and stable potential-resource order
patient repetition and whole-day time shifts
one pass of medication additions or replacements
transformations.selectionAuthority: Unselected resources are never emitted; disabled transformations do not resurrect resources. Reference-only modes may reference external resources.
transformations.missingMedicationData: omit; do not invent values or DAR
transformations.identifierStability: Selection cannot renumber retained resource IDs or generated identifier counters.
transformations.medicationActionPass: After request replacement, take one snapshot of MedicationAdministration and MedicationStatement resources. Apply exactly one selected action per source: retain, add the other type while retaining the source, or replace the source with the other type. Newly produced resources are not processed again in this pass. Both directions may be selected; they operate on the snapshot without recursion. Targets require selected output resources and receive distinct IDs.

additionalIdentifiers.stableRuleId: Persist a UUID when the rule is created; preserve it when editing or importing.
additionalIdentifiers.counterScope: one per rule across eligible resource types and repetitions
additionalIdentifiers.counterOrder: stable potential-resource sequence independent of output selection
additionalIdentifiers.hashEncoding: For each hashContext component in the listed order, concatenate ASCII decimal UTF-8 byte length, a colon, and the UTF-8 bytes. UUID uses canonical lowercase spelling; iteration uses its nonnegative decimal index.
additionalIdentifiers.uniqueness: system/value across distinct logical resources and iterations; case-scoped rules permit sharing within the same effective patient/facility case
additionalIdentifiers.duplicateSerialization: same logical resource in multiple formats is counted once
additionalIdentifiers.collision: stop with rule and conflicting resource identities
additionalIdentifiers.security: Deterministic hash identifiers do not guarantee secure pseudonymization.

tokens.count:0N: Minimum width N with leading zeros, for example count:08; longer values are not truncated
tokens.patientId: Effective patient ID for this repetition
tokens.hash: First 32 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256 over the fixed hash context

additionalIdentifiers.invalidPattern: Reject unknown tokens, unmatched braces and malformed padding; no expression evaluation.

caseScope.identity: effective patient and original facility case number
caseScope.missingCase: omit identifier with an import-report output-selection note
caseScope.collision: allow sharing within the same case; reject across cases

profileBaseline.rule: Use a profile only when the emitted resource claims it; package releases are separate from terminology years.

configuration.conflictingDuplicate: reject; do not silently apply last value
configuration.disabledSelection: retain stored value; compute effective disabled state in Java; no implicit fallback
configuration.profileNames: configuration profiles are separate from FHIR StructureDefinitions
configuration.executionSettings: parallelism and environment selection are separate from clinical options

encounterClasses.otherClasses: preserve existing behavior; no new class mapping
encounterClasses.assignmentTieBreak: latest start not after event timestamp, then input row

legacyOnlyJavaProperties.name: ADD_MISSING_DIAGNOSES_FROM_SUPER_ENCOUNTER
legacyOnlyJavaProperties.reason: Unversioned input only; versioned configuration assigns diagnosis references automatically using selected roles, levels and temporal matching.
